questions.question: In instruction-level parallelism (ILP) architecture design, what is the fundamental operational difference between a Very Long Instruction Word (VLIW) processor and a dynamically scheduled superscalar processor?
options: VLIW processors rely on compile-time static scheduling and dependency analysis to issue multiple operations per cycle, eliminating dynamic instruction dispatch and hazard-detection hardware.
VLIW processors execute multiple independent threads simultaneously across execution units, whereas superscalar processors execute only one thread at a time.
Superscalar processors compile instructions into fixed multi-operation packets, whereas VLIW processors decode variable-length instructions dynamically at runtime.
VLIW processors require dynamic out-of-order execution buffers to reorder operations inside the long instruction word prior to execution.
Superscalar processors execute exclusively RISC instructions, whereas VLIW processors are fundamentally restricted to CISC instruction sets.

questions.question: In CMOS digital circuit design, why is a full transmission gate constructed by connecting an NMOS transistor and a PMOS transistor in parallel, rather than using a single NMOS pass transistor?
options: A single NMOS transistor cannot be switched completely off, causing unacceptable subthreshold leakage current across the node.
An NMOS pass transistor passes a strong logic '0' but degrades a logic '1' by a threshold voltage drop (VDD - Vtn), while the PMOS transistor passes a strong logic '1'.
Paralleling NMOS and PMOS transistors is strictly required to suppress parasitic substrate latch-up during high-frequency switching.
An NMOS transistor exhibits significantly higher input gate capacitance, which slows down clock transitions when used without a complementary PMOS device.
A complementary PMOS transistor is necessary to actively sink current and ground the output node when the control signal is de-asserted.

questions.question: In digital arithmetic circuit design, what structural technique allows a Wallace tree multiplier to achieve an O(log n) critical path latency compared to the O(n) latency of a standard array multiplier?
options: It serializes partial product accumulation using high-frequency dynamic shift registers.
It completely bypasses partial product generation by using precomputed radix-1024 lookup tables.
It employs trees of carry-save adders (CSAs) to reduce partial product rows concurrently without propagating carries until the final two-operand addition.
It replaces conventional full adders with synchronous accumulator registers clocked at twice the core system frequency.
It duplicates arithmetic units across multiple asynchronous clock domains to compute partial additions redundantly.

questions.question: In shared-memory multiprocessor system architecture, why do directory-based cache coherence protocols scale to significantly higher core counts than bus-based snooping protocols?
options: Directory-based protocols eliminate the necessity of cache invalidation and update messages when modifying shared cache blocks.
Snooping protocols require centralized serialization at the DRAM interface that causes severe contention at physically distributed memory banks.
Directory-based protocols convert write-back caches into write-through caches, thereby removing data races across the network.
Directory-based protocols avoid broadcast traffic by tracking the sharing state of cache lines and sending targeted point-to-point coherence messages only to relevant nodes.
Snooping protocols are architecturally incompatible with invalidation-based coherence states such as MESI and MOESI.

questions.question: In instruction-level parallel processor microarchitecture, what is the primary operational distinction between a CDC 6600-style Scoreboard and Tomasulo's algorithm regarding the handling of data hazards?
options: Scoreboarding eliminates RAW hazards using hardware data forwarding, whereas Tomasulo's algorithm stalls the pipeline until operands are written to the register file.
Tomasulo's algorithm relies on static compiler scheduling to detect write hazards, whereas Scoreboarding relies strictly on dynamic hardware detection.
Scoreboarding operates out-of-order while issuing instructions, whereas Tomasulo's algorithm enforces in-order issue, execution, and retirement.
Tomasulo's algorithm handles only fixed-point integer pipelines, whereas Scoreboarding was developed specifically for out-of-order SIMD vector processing.

Scoreboarding stalls instruction progression on WAR and WAW hazards, whereas Tomasulo's algorithm dynamically eliminates WAR and WAW hazards through implicit register renaming via reservation stations and the Common Data Bus (CDB).
